A0700.situation: derived on the heights: Allied ≈ 40,915 plotted strength unchangedThe reconstruction plots formations, not losses. A holding that does not change does not mean the fighting there has stopped.The Allied columns begin to leave the plateau (the hour is disputed)Every column that goes down into the valley is a column no longer holding the centre.
A0700.dispatch: 07:00 - 08:00 / The Allied left opens the battle / Kienmayer's Austrian advance guard attacks Telnitz, the southernmost village on the Goldbach. Legrand's thin line holds the buildings and the vineyard bank above them, and the village changes hands repeatedly. Behind Kienmayer, Dokhturov's I Column is coming down off the southern end of the plateau. / c. 07:00Kienmayer's advance guard attacks Telnitz. According to Stutterheim the musket fire there grew very murderous, and the Szekler infantry regiment lost two thirds of its men, dead and wounded.c. 07:00Dokhturov's I Column leaves its camp as the disposition ordered; Kutuzov's report has it force the enemy back to Telnitz about eight, and Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky has Dokhturov begin the attack on Telnitz at half past eight. / WHAT CHANGED AT 07:00Contests Telnitz house by house against KienmayerMarching from Raigern toward TelnitzAttacks Telnitz; the village changes hands several timesLeaves its camp at seven, as the disposition ordered, and descends toward the Goldbach (Buxhowden's and Kutuzov's reports)The Santon detachment holdingSecond Column advancingThird Column advancing

fresh0400.dispatch: 04:00 - 07:00 / Dispositions in the dark / Napoleon has deliberately given up the Pratzen plateau and left his right, along the lower Goldbach, looking thin enough to invite attack. Weyrother's Allied orders, read out at Krzenowitz after midnight to commanders who largely did not understand them, send four of five columns south-west across the French front. Fog fills the Goldbach valley. Soult's two assault divisions are standing in it, invisible from the heights. / c. 01:00Weyrother reads the dispositions at Allied headquarters, Krzenowitz. Kutuzov reportedly dozes.c. 04:00The disposition orders the Allied columns to march at seven; Thiébault records reports through the night of the Allied left moving, judged by the noise. Liechtenstein's cavalry, misplaced on the left, must counter-march north across the front of the 4th Column; the Materialien has it ordered off only at dawn.before dawnNapoleon mounted at one in the morning to ride round his posts (the 30th Bulletin), and Thiébault has him on horseback long before day; the dispositions called his marshals to his bivouac for half past seven. His post, 'la butte' of the orders, is taken here to be the Zuran; the map places him there from 04:00, and the hour he took post is not established. / WHAT CHANGED AT 04:00On the height of his bivouac, taken here to be the Zuran: 'la butte' of the orders of 1 December, 'the barrow by Schlapanitz' in Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky. The dispositions call his marshals to his bivouac for the morning's ordersStanding in fog behind Puntowitz, which hid it from the plateauConcealed by the fog in the valley behind GirzikowitzStrung out along the stream; skirmishing through the nightAt Raigern since the night of 1 December, 8 km south-west of Telnitz and just beyond the map edge, after about 115 km from Vienna in under two days in Sokolov, thirty-six leagues in forty-eight hours in Thiers, a march whose figures vary between the sourcesFormed on the right of V Corps, linking toward BernadotteFormed south of the road, on its right as ordered the evening before, level with the fortified hill
